item.title: Game Boy Emulator
item.description: A Game Boy (DMG) emulator written in C++, built from scratch to understand the CPU, memory system, graphics, and interrupts.

item.title: 6502 Emulator
item.description: A cycle-counted NMOS 6502 emulator with memory-mapped I/O, interrupts, and a real ca65/ld65 assembler toolchain. Passes the Klaus Dormann functional test suite.

item.title: myos
item.description: A tiny x86 OS built from a 512-byte boot sector up — real mode to protected mode, GDT setup, and a path toward a real kernel.

item.title: Smartwatch Firmware
item.description: ESP-IDF firmware for a DIY smartwatch driving a GC9A01 240x240 round SPI display, with a from-scratch display driver.

item.title: Notes on Emulating the Game Boy PPU
item.description: Writing the pixel pipeline was the part of the Game Boy emulator that took the longest to get cycle-accurate. This post walks through how the background FIFO, sprite fetcher, and mode-3 timing fit together, and the test ROMs that finally caught my off-by-one scanline bug.

item.title: Getting NMI/IRQ Timing Right on the 6502
item.description: The Klaus Dormann test suite doesn’t check interrupt timing, so my 6502 core passed the functional tests while still being subtly wrong about when interrupts could fire relative to instruction boundaries. Here’s how I found and fixed it.

item.title: From 512 Bytes to Protected Mode: Booting myos
item.description: A walkthrough of the boot sector, the jump to a second-stage loader, enabling A20, building a GDT by hand, and the first far jump into 32-bit protected mode.

item.title: Writing a Display Driver for a Round SPI Screen
item.description: The GC9A01 datasheet is short on examples, so this is the driver I wish existed when I started the smartwatch firmware — SPI setup, init sequence, and a fast framebuffer flush routine on ESP-IDF.
